pages.title: Grade 6-11 Resources
pages.metaTitle: Grade 6-11 English resources and syllabus practice
pages.description: Interactive English practice for Grades 6 to 11, with three activities for each grade built from the competency levels of the school syllabus for that grade.
pages.keywords: grade 6 english, grade 7 english, grade 8 english, grade 9 english, grade 10 english, grade 11 english, competency levels, syllabus practice, Sri Lanka

hero.text: Interactive English practice for Grades 6 to 11. Each grade provides three interactive language activities and five complete listening tests, every one of them aligned with a numbered competency level from the syllabus that grade actually follows. Everything marks itself and explains the answer.

blocks.title: Where these activities come from
text: Every activity on these pages is built from **the competency levels of the school syllabus**, not from examination papers. Each one names the competency level it practises, so you can check it against your own term notes.

Note that Grades 6 and 7 are not following the same syllabus. **Grade 6 has moved to the new 2026 syllabus**, which is organised by skill — listening, speaking, reading, writing and literary appreciation — and is grouped around text types rather than grammar topics. **Grades 7 to 11 remain on the earlier syllabus**, built around eight competencies covering sounds, mechanics of writing, listening, vocabulary, reading, grammar, written communication and speaking.
This matters when comparing grades: the same number means different things on either side of that line. Competency level 5.4 in Grade 8 is not competency level 5.4 in Grade 6.

The listening tests are read aloud using the English voice your own device provides, so the voices may sound different on a computer and on a phone. The words and the questions are the same everywhere.

hero.text: Grade 6 follows the new 2026 syllabus, which is organised by skill rather than by grammar topic. These activities cover listening, reading a functional text, writing in an official context, and reading a literary text. Each one names the competency level it practises.

blocks.title: Grade 6 is on the new syllabus
text: From 2026, Grade 6 works to a syllabus organised around five competencies — listening, speaking, reading, writing and literary appreciation — with texts grouped as functional, informational or literary. The competency numbers here do not match those used in Grades 7 to 11.

blocks.heading: Grade 6 English practice
intro: Reading a timetable, filling in a form, and reading a simple poem. These follow competency levels 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6 and 4.1 of the 2026 syllabus.

blocks.heading: Grade 6 Game Zone
intro: Short drag-and-drop and word-order games for the grammar focuses Grade 6 still needs: nouns, *is / are / was / were*, articles and prepositions. They sit beside the practice activities above — not instead of them.

items.title: Wordshake
items.text: Sixty seconds to make as many three and four letter words as you can from sixteen letters. Builds vocabulary and spelling together.

items.title: Open Grade 6 Game Zone

blocks.heading: Grade 6 Pupil's Book Listening Tests
intro: The listening activities from your English textbook, as tests you can do on your own. Your teacher usually reads these texts aloud in class; here your device reads them, so you can listen again at home, check your answers and see the text afterwards.
The activities follow the Grade 6 English Pupil's Book printed from 2014 to 2019, and one Workbook activity. If your class uses a newer book, the unit and activity numbers may differ.

blocks.heading: Grade 6 Extra Listening Tests
intro: Five extra listening tests written by RCF English, for practice beyond the textbook: short conversations, an announcement, a description and a story. The passage is read aloud by your own browser, so there is nothing to download.

Choose **Practice** to replay as often as you like, or **Formal test** for examination conditions, where the recording plays twice only. You can change the reading speed, and there are five words to learn before you listen. In Practice you can open the transcript if you are stuck; in a Formal test it appears only after you submit. Every test can be printed as a worksheet, and all of them, with the Pupil's Book activities, are together in the [Listening Laboratory](listening-lab/). These follow competency levels 1.1 to 1.6 of the 2026 syllabus.

pages.title: Wordshake: the Grade 6 Vocabulary Game
pages.metaTitle: Wordshake: Free Grade 6 English Vocabulary Game
pages.description: A free word game for Grade 6 English: make three and four letter words from sixteen letters in sixty seconds. Works on a phone, and needs no account.
pages.keywords: grade 6 english game, vocabulary game, english word game for students, word building game, spelling game grade 6

hero.text: Sixteen letters, sixty seconds. Make as many three and four letter words as you can - the longer the word, the more it scores.

blocks.heading: How to play
text: Tap the letters one after another to build a word, then send it. If it is a real English word you get ten points for every letter. If it is not, nothing is lost - try another.
bullets: **Three letters score 30, four letters score 40.** Longer words are always worth more, so look for a fourth letter before you send a three-letter word.
**A letter can only be taken back from the end.** Tap the last letter again to remove it, or use *Clear* to start the word afresh.
**The same word only counts once.** After that, the game tells you that you already have it.
**You can play with the keyboard.** Move between the letters with the Tab key, choose one with Enter or the space bar, and press Enter anywhere else to send the word.

blocks.heading: Getting better at it
text: The score comes from noticing patterns, not from typing quickly.
bullets: **Start with the vowels.** Five of the sixteen letters are vowels. Find them first, then look for consonants that sit either side.
**Work in families.** If AT is there, try BAT, CAT, FAT, HAT, MAT, PAT, RAT, SAT. One pattern often gives four or five words.
**Add a letter to a word you already have.** CAR becomes CARD or CART; EAT becomes HEAT, MEAT, NEAT, SEAT.
**Do not stare at one word.** When nothing comes, clear it and look somewhere else on the grid. The clock does not stop.

blocks.title: For teachers
text: This works well on a classroom screen with the class calling out words, and as a five-minute warmer at the start of a lesson. It needs no preparation, no login and no internet connection once the page has loaded.
The word list holds about 1,200 three and four letter words. A word the class knows may occasionally be missing - if you find one, [tell us](corrections/) and it will be added.

hero.text: The O/L year. Grade 11 consolidates rather than introduces: the conditionals are brought together, reported speech is extended to questions and commands, and word building is revisited. All three are areas where marks are thrown away by habit rather than by difficulty.

intro: The listening activities from your English textbook, as tests you can do on your own. Your teacher usually reads these texts aloud in class; here your device reads them, so you can listen again at home, check your answers and see the text afterwards.

Each test names the chapter and activity in the Grade 11 Pupil's Book or Workbook. The two stress activities (Pupil's Book Chapter 8 and Workbook Chapter 4) are not here, because a device voice cannot stress a chosen word.

blocks.heading: Grade 11 Extra Listening Tests
intro: Five extra listening tests written by RCF English, at the hardest level on the site: a formal debate, a careers talk, an interview in which much is implied, a committee meeting, and examination advice.

Choose **Practice** to replay freely, or **Formal test** for examination conditions. Each test starts with five words to learn. In Practice you can open the transcript if you are stuck; in a Formal test it appears only after you submit. Every test prints as a worksheet, and all of them, with the Pupil's Book activities, are together in the [Listening Laboratory](listening-lab/). These follow competency levels 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8, with inference at 5.7 and 5.8.
